text:
Hannah: Quick postmortem follow-up thread for GPU capacity/autoscale. We need owners for the action items: quota guardrail, scheduler tuning (eviction budgets + packing), and headroom visibility. Keep updates short here.
Omar: I'll take scheduler tuning. My immediate plan: introduce an eviction_budget per pool, tighten packing thresholds to reduce fragmentation, and add a short-lived prewarm pool for model cold starts. Canary in staging next 48h.
Zoe: I'll own quota coordination with finance/cloud. Two asks: an emergency safety buffer (up to +10% reserved for 7 days) and a conservative longer-term commit (+8%). I'll open the ticket with cost delta and SLA impact.
Grant: I'll update the runbook + oncall playbook. Adding a quick-reserve command, an elastic preemption checklist, and a decision tree for routing to fallback models. Also adding example logs to help triage.
Omar: Scheduler snippet I'm testing in staging (KEDA-style scaler):
```yaml
apiVersion: keda.sh/v1alpha1
kind: ScaledObject
metadata:
  name: gpu-batch-scaledobject
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    name: embeddings-deployment
  triggers:
  - type: prometheus
    metadata:
      serverAddress: http://prom:9090
      metricName: gpu_util_pct
      threshold: "80"
  pollingInterval: 15
  cooldownPeriod: 300
```
Omar: Increasing cooldownPeriod to 300s to avoid rapid scale cycles during short spikes.
Hannah: Good. Add an eviction_budget metric so we can see how many GPUs are reserved for preemptible vs guaranteed workloads.
Zoe: capacity-bot created ticket https://redwood.local/tickets/INC-4701 for emergency buffer request and TASK-9500 for scheduler canary.
capacity-bot: Reminder: INC-4701 created by Zoe; status: awaiting finance review. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
Grant: Two recurring patterns I documented: 1) nightly bulk embeddings from analytics that bypass rate limits, 2) cold-start churn when new model versions deploy. I'll add sample traces to the runbook.
Omar: For nightly jobs, I recommend a soft admission controller that tags and delays large batches to off-peak windows, but also a hard quota guard to protect SLOs. I'll draft both.
Zoe: If admission change is slow, we fallback to the emergency buffer to avoid customer impact. Finance wants exact cost exposure; I'll attach recent token counts and estimated GPU hours.
Hannah: Observability ask: add pool_headroom_gpus and eviction_budget_ratio to Console and a 15m alert when headroom_gpus < 5 for 2 consecutive windows. Also a daily report on pools with headroom < 10% so product can evaluate whether to move customers.
Omar: I'll instrument those metrics in the next deploy (2026-04-06) and wire alerts (2026-04-07).
Hannah: Owners & dates recap: Omar - scheduler canary + metrics (canary 2026-03-31, metrics deploy 2026-04-06), Zoe - quota emergency ticket (2026-03-29) + commit PR (2026-04-08), Grant - runbook + oncall edits (2026-03-28). I'll schedule a 10m closure check on 2026-04-05.
Grant: Adding a weekend 48h surge sim to validate eviction behavior. I'll coordinate for weekend 2026-04-04 and include a post-sim template.
Zoe: capacity-bot updated action tracker: INC-4701, TASK-9500, TASK-9501 (runbook update), TASK-9502 (surge-sim).
capacity-bot: Action tracker updated: INC-4701, TASK-9500, TASK-9501, TASK-9502.
Hannah: If we still see repeated headroom alerts after these items, escalate to capacity oncall and consider temporary routing limits for non-critical orgs. Thanks all ":thumbsup:"
Omar: Starting canary today in staging and will post results here.
Zoe: Filing finance note now.
Grant: Will open the runbook PR after adding traces.
